definitions.explanation: Describes something that is conspicuously new and unused, with the freshness still clearly visible. Emphasizes the appearance of newness more than the fact of being new.

examples.japanese: {真新|まあたら}しい⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{履|は}く→履く：00700_haku⟧。
{真新|まあたら}しい⟦{制服|せいふく}→制服：03086_seifuku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{袖|そで}→袖：02217_sode⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}した→通す：02300_toosu⟧。
examples.english: I put on a brand new uniform for the first time.

examples.japanese: {真新|まあたら}しい⟦ビル→ビル：01500_biru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{建|た}ち{並|なら}んでいる→建ち並ぶ：20170_tachinarabu⟧。
examples.english: Brand new buildings stand lined up in front of the station.

notes:
USAGE:
Unlike ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧, which simply means "new," {真新|まあたら}しい emphasizes that something looks visibly fresh and untouched. It often describes physical objects like clothing, buildings, and equipment. The prefix {真|ま}～ intensifies the base adjective.

WRITING:
{真|ま} is an intensifying prefix meaning "truly" and ⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧ means "new." Together they convey "truly/completely new."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真新|まあたら}しい⟦{靴|くつ}→靴：00725_kutsu⟧: brand new shoes
- {真新|まあたら}しい⟦{制服|せいふく}→制服：03086_seifuku⟧: brand new uniform
- {真新|まあたら}しい⟦{教科書|きょうかしょ}→教科書：01085_kyoukasho⟧: brand new textbook
